body.translated_text: <s>Vasudhārādhāraṇīsūtra</s> (The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the Stream of Wealth)
Oṃ! Homage to the Noble and Glorious Lady <s>Vasudhārā</s>!

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān kośāmbyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ viharati sma | kaṇṭakasaṃjñake mahāvanavare ghoṣitārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhaṃ pañcamātrair bhikṣuśataiḥ saṃbahulaiś ca śrāvakair asaṃkhyayaiś ca bodhisattvaiḥ sarvabuddhaguṇasamanvāgataiḥ | tatra khalu bhagavāṃs tasyām eva parṣadi tair eva parivṛtaḥ puraskṛtaḥ sarvadāridryavyādhiduḥkhārṇavapariśoṣaṇaṃ nāma dharmaparyāyaṃ deśayati sma | ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇaṃ svarthaṃ suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ saṃprakāśayati sma |
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling in the great city of <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, in the excellent great forest called <s>Kaṇṭakasaṃjñaka</s>, in the <s>Ghoṣita</s> park, together with a great assembly of monks — five hundred monks in number — along with numerous <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples) and innumerable <s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with all the qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>. Thereupon, the Blessed One, in that very assembly, surrounded and attended by them, was teaching a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> called 'The Drying Up of the Ocean of All Poverty, Disease, and Suffering.' He was proclaiming the holy life (<s>brahmacaryam</s>) — excellent in the beginning, excellent in the middle, excellent at the end, good in meaning, good in expression, complete, perfect, pure, and stainless.

body.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena kauśāmbyāṃ mahānagaryāṃ sucandro nāma gṛhapatiḥ prativasati sma | upaśāntendriyopaśāntamānaso bahuputro bahuduhitaro bahubhṛtyajanasaṃpannaḥ śrāddho mahāśrāddhaḥ | tena khalu punaḥ samayena yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantam anekaśatasahasraṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ekānte nyaṣīdat | ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ sucandro nāma gṛhapatir bhagavantam etad avocat | pṛccheyam ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ tathāgataṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ kiñcid eva pradeśaṃ sacen me bhagavān avakāśaṃ kuryāt pṛṣṭapraśnavyākaraṇāya | evam ukte bhagavān sucandragṛhapatim etad avocat | pṛccha tvaṃ gṛhapate yad yad evākāṃkṣasyan te tatra praśnavyākaraṇena cittam ārādhayiṣye | evam ukte sucandro gṛhapatiḥ sādhu bhagavann iti bhagavato vacanaṃ pratiśrutya bhagavantam etad avocat | kathaṃ bhagavan kulaputro vā kuladuhitā vā daridro bhūtvā adaridro bhavati | vyādhitaś ca bhūtvā avyādhito bhavati | atha khalu bhagavān jānann eva sucandraṃ gṛhapatim etad avocat | kim iti tvaṃ gṛhapate daridratāyāḥ paripraśnaṃ pṛcchasi?
body.translated_text: Now at that time, in the great city of <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, there lived a householder named <s>Sucandra</s> — with pacified faculties and pacified mind, having many sons and many daughters, endowed with many servants and attendants, faithful and greatly devoted. At that time, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached and bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, having circumambulated the Blessed One many hundreds of thousands of times, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder <s>Sucandra</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: "I wish to ask the Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, about a certain matter, if the Blessed One would grant me the opportunity to answer my question." Thus addressed, the Blessed One spoke to the householder <s>Sucandra</s>: "Ask, O householder, whatever you wish — I shall satisfy your mind with the answer to your question." Thus addressed, the householder <s>Sucandra</s>, saying "Excellent, O Blessed One!" and having assented to the Blessed One's words, spoke thus to the Blessed One: "How, O Blessed One, does a son of good family or a daughter of good family, having been poor, become free from poverty? And having been afflicted with disease, become free from disease?" Then the Blessed One, knowing full well, spoke thus to the householder <s>Sucandra</s>: "Why, O householder, do you ask about poverty?"

body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One, with a <s>Brahma</s>-voice that fulfills all wishes, said to the householder <s>Sucandra</s>: 'There was, householder, in the past, in ages innumerable <s>kalpas</s> ago — at that time, at that moment, there arose in the world a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Awakened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>) named <s>Śrīvajradharasāgaranirghoṣa</s> (Glorious Thundering Ocean of the Vajra-Bearer), endowed with knowledge and conduct, a <s>Sugata</s>, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed Charioteer of Persons to be Tamed, Teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>, a Blessed One. In the presence of that <s>Tathāgata</s>, householder, I heard the <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Vasudhārā</s>. Having heard it, I grasped it, retained it, recited it, taught it, mastered it, approved it, and made it known in detail to others. I too shall now teach you, O son of good family, that <s>dhāraṇī</s> in the same way. By the power of this <s>dhāraṇī</s>, O son of good family: humans do not cause harm; non-humans do not cause harm; <s>devas</s> do not cause harm; <s>nāgas</s> do not cause harm; <s>yakṣas</s> do not cause harm; <s>asuras</s> do not cause harm; <s>rākṣasas</s> do not cause harm; <s>bhūtas</s> do not cause harm; <s>pretas</s> do not cause harm; <s>piśācas</s> do not cause harm; <s>kumbhāṇḍas</s> do not cause harm; <s>ostāḍakas</s> do not cause harm; <s>apasmāras</s> (epilepsy-spirits) do not cause harm; <s>gandharvas</s> do not cause harm; <s>kinnaras</s> do not cause harm; <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents) do not cause harm; <s>pūtanās</s> do not cause harm; <s>kaṭapūtanās</s> do not cause harm; all <s>grahas</s> (seizing spirits) do not cause harm; all <s>devas</s> do not cause harm; hunger and thirst do not cause harm; all [beings that] feed [on various things] do not cause harm. Thus, up to: those that feed on flowers, those that feed on fruits, those that feed on leaves, those that feed on bark, those that feed on trunks, those that feed on roots, those that feed on fragrances, those that feed on incense, those that feed on lamps, those that feed on garlands, those that feed on oblations — none cause harm. Those that feed on vitality, those that feed on sweat, those that feed on fluids, those that feed on blood, those that feed on flesh, those that feed on fat, those that feed on bones, those that feed on marrow, those that feed on gore, those that feed on semen, those that feed on life-force — none of them cause harm. Thus, up to: those that feed on excrement, those that feed on urine, those that feed on phlegm, those that feed on mucus, those that feed on moisture, those that feed on slime, those that feed on leftovers, those that feed on non-leftovers, those that feed on remnants — none cause harm. Those that feed on crops, those that feed on embryos — none of them cause harm. All <s>ḍākinīs</s> do not cause harm. Shadows do not cause harm. The born do not cause harm. Those that feed on meditation do not cause harm. children.translated_text: ) To those who have attained the foremost pair, to those who have attained the auspicious pair, to the Blessed Ones from <s>Vipaśyin</s> onward to <s>Śākyamuni</s>, who have fulfilled the perfection of giving (<s>dānapāramitā</s>): by the splendor of <s>Vipaśyin</s>; by the miraculous power of <s>Śikhin</s>; by the wisdom of <s>Viśvabhuk</s>; by the strength of <s>Krakucchanda</s>; by the training of <s>Kanakamuni</s>; by the virtues of <s>Kāśyapa</s>; by the heroic energy of the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>; and by the vow of <s>Maitreya</s> — may these <s>mantra</s>-words of the <s>Tathāgata</s> bring me success! This <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge) benefits all beings, liberating them from the ocean of poverty, disease, suffering, and misfortune. I shall now proclaim this secret <s>vidyā</s>, the <s>dhāraṇī</s> called <s>Vasudhārā</s>. I recollect the <s>mantra</s>-words of the meaning spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s>. They are as follows: Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ! Oṃ śrīdhane śrīdhane! O Lady of Wealth and Sovereignty! O Radiant One! O Inexhaustible Treasury! O Producer of What Is Wished For in the Mind! O Fulfiller of the Mind's Desires! O Accomplisher! O Koṭe koṭe! O Sovereign of Koṭīs! O Mistress of Koṭīs! O Bringer of Infinite and Boundless Jewels, Garments, Ornaments, and Adornments! O Increaser of Wealth and Grain! O Gatherer of What Is Wished For! O Milker of <s>Śakra</s>'s Treasuries and Storehouses! O Seizer of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>'s <s>mantras</s>! By the <s>Buddha</s>, by the <s>Buddha</s>! By the truth of the <s>Buddha</s>! By the truth of the <s>Dharma</s>! By the truth of the <s>Saṃgha</s>! By the truth of all <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>! By the truth of the provisions for awakening (<s>bodhiprāgbhāra</s>)! By the truth of all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>! By the truth of <s>Brahmā</s>! By the truth of <s>Viṣṇu</s>! By the truth of <s>Rudra</s>! By the truth of the World-Protectors (<s>Lokapālas</s>)! O Fulfiller of the Wealth-Lord's Command! For the prosperity of silver, gold, gems, pearls, diamonds, <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, conch, crystal, coral, gold, silver, emeralds, rubies, cat's-eye, and all precious substances! In whichever direction this <s>vidyā</s> (sacred knowledge) is retained, that direction becomes worthy of worship. In whatever place it is worshipped for the purpose of prosperity (<s>pauṣṭika</s>) — whether in one's own house or another's house — with faith and supreme faith, one should spread out before [oneself] an image of <s>Vasudhārā</s>, or a statue of the Venerable Lady, or a painting, and make a four-cornered <s>maṇḍala</s> with sandalwood, adorned with flowers, incense, lamps, fragrance, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, parasols, banners, bells, and flags, and make offerings according to one's means with <s>bali</s> oblations, food offerings, and various services. The <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor) likewise, with [the same] observance, should worship three times in the night and three times during the day, with all <s>bali</s> oblations and offerings. body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: "Go, <s>Ānanda</s>, to the house of the householder <s>Sucandra</s> and see it abundantly filled with all wealth and grain, with all gems and gold, and with all provisions — the great treasuries and storehouses all completely filled." Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, having assented to the Blessed One's words, went to the great city of <s>Kauśāmbī</s>, to the dwelling of <s>Sucandra</s>, and approached his house. Having approached and entered inside, he beheld it abundantly filled with all wealth and grain, and the great treasuries and storehouses all completely filled. Having seen this, delighted, pleased, elated, joyful, filled with gladness and happiness, he approached the Blessed One. Having approached, the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, amazed and filled with gladness and happiness, bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and spoke thus to the Blessed One: "What (

body.text: atha khalv āyuṣmān ānanda utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya kṛtakarapuṭo bhūtvā bhagavataḥ mukham avalokya yadīdānīṃ tasyāṃ velāyām imāṃ gāthā abhāṣat |

children.text: āpūrṇam asmin gṛheṣu maṇḍalaṃ namo 'stu te śrīvasudhāraṇī sadā ||

body.text: atha khalv āyuṣmān ānando imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ bhagavato 'ntikāt śrutvā hṛṣṭatuṣṭa udagra āttamanāḥ pramuditā prītisaumanasyajāto bhagavantam etad avocat | ko nāmāyaṃ bhagavanta dharmaparyāyaḥ kathaṃ bhagavan dhārayāmy enaṃ dharmaparyāyam | bhagavān āha ḥ sucandragṛhapatiparipṛcchety api ānanda dhāraya sarvadhanadhānyahiraṇyasuvarṇaratnanidhānam ity api dhāraya sarvatathāgatapraśastety api dhāraya sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhitā vasudhārādhāraṇīkalpam ity api dhāraya |
idam avocad bhagavān āttamanā āyuṣmān ānandas te ca bhikṣavas te ca bodhisattvā mahāsattvāḥ sā ca sarvāvatī parṣat sadevamānuṣāsuragaruḍagandharvaś ca loko bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti |
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. The joyful venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, those monks, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and <s>Mahāsattvas</s>, that entire assembly, and the whole world with its gods, humans, <s>asuras</s>, <s>garuḍas</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s> rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.
The Noble and Glorious <s>Vasudhārā-nāma-dhāraṇī-parisūtra</s> (The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī called Vasudhārā) is complete.

children.text: ye dharmā hetuprabhavā hetuṃ teṣāṃ tathāgato hy avadat |
children.translated_text: Those <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) which arise from causes — the <s>Tathāgata</s> has declared their cause,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca yo nirodha evaṃvādī mahāśramaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and that which is their cessation — thus speaks the Great Ascetic (<s>Mahāśramaṇa</s>).
